postTitle: Moving Countries: Rebuilding Your Financial Identity
topic: Sending money home: the same €300 a month costs very different amounts by provider

assumptions.notes: Worked example from the post. A household sends €300 a month for 10 years. At 6.5% per transfer (around the global average): €19.50 a month, €234 a year, €2,340 over 10 years. At 2% (a competitive digital provider): €6 a month, €72 a year, €720 over 10 years. Difference: €13.50 a month, €162 a year, €1,620 over 10 years, which is 5.4 months of the €300 transfer. No growth or inflation applied. Costs vary by route and provider.

hookVariants.narration: Sending three hundred euros home monthly? Over ten years, costs can differ by sixteen hundred and twenty euros.
A transfer home with zero fees can still be expensive. The cost hides in the exchange rate.
Sending money home to family is one of the most overpriced transactions in everyday finance.

beats.narration: Take a household sending three hundred euros home every month, for ten years. Same family, same route.
At six and a half percent per transfer, around the global average, the costs come to two thousand three hundred and forty euros.
At two percent, a price some competitive digital providers charge, they come to seven hundred and twenty euros.
The difference is sixteen hundred and twenty euros. More than five months of the transfer itself, buying nothing.
beats.subtext: More than five months of transfers

beats.narration: And the fee is only part of it. The exchange rate margin is rarely shown, and is often the larger cost.
beats.subtext: The exchange rate margin, rarely shown

beats.narration: So compare one number. Fix the amount, check three providers on your route, and see what actually arrives.
